blocks.title: Disease and pathogens
blocks.md:
A **disease** is a disorder of the body or mind. An **infectious disease** is caused by a **pathogen** that passes from one host to another.

- **Bacteria**: cholera, typhoid, tuberculosis.
- **Viruses**: HIV, influenza, measles.
- **Protoctists** (single-celled): malaria (*Plasmodium*).
- **Fungi**: ringworm, athlete's foot.

A **vector** is an organism that carries a pathogen from one host to another.

blocks.title: Malaria
blocks.md:
**Malaria** is caused by *Plasmodium* and carried by the **female *Anopheles* mosquito**. The parasite infects the liver and the **red blood cells**, which burst at intervals.

**Symptoms**: high fever, shivering, sweating, headache, tiredness, anaemia. Severe malaria, especially in young children and pregnant women, can be fatal.

blocks.caption: Transmission of malaria.
blocks.alt: Four boxes with arrows: an infected person with parasites in the blood, a female Anopheles that bites and takes blood, the parasite growing in the mosquito, the mosquito biting a new person.

blocks.title: Preventing malaria
blocks.md:
- Sleep under an **insecticide-treated mosquito net**.
- Remove or cover **stagnant water** (tins, tyres, blocked gutters) where mosquitoes lay eggs; clear bushes around houses.
- Use screens on windows and repellents; indoor spraying where recommended.
- Preventive medicine for pregnant women and young children as advised by health services.

blocks.title: Treatment (flag for health review)
blocks.md: Anyone with fever should go to a health centre for a **test**. Treatment uses **antimalarial drugs** prescribed by a health worker, and the whole course must be taken. Antibiotics do not work against malaria because the parasite is not a bacterium.

blocks.title: Find the vector
blocks.statement: A family lives near a swamp in Douala. Several children have fever and shivering. Name the pathogen, the vector and one prevention method.
steps: The disease is malaria; the pathogen is *Plasmodium*.
The vector is the female *Anopheles* mosquito; they should sleep under treated nets and drain stagnant water.

blocks.title: Why drain puddles?
blocks.statement: Explain why clearing stagnant water reduces malaria cases.
steps: Mosquito eggs, larvae and pupae live in still water.
Without breeding sites fewer mosquitoes survive, so fewer people are bitten and the parasite is passed on less.

blocks.title: Water-borne diseases
blocks.md:
**Cholera** (the bacterium *Vibrio cholerae*) and **typhoid** (*Salmonella* Typhi) spread by **contaminated water and food**, usually where sewage mixes with drinking water.

- **Cholera**: sudden watery diarrhoea and vomiting that can cause fatal **dehydration**. Treatment: **oral rehydration solution** (clean water with salts and sugar) and medical care.
- **Typhoid**: prolonged fever, headache, stomach pain.

blocks.title: Tuberculosis (TB)
blocks.md: **TB** (*Mycobacterium tuberculosis*) infects the lungs. It spreads through **droplets** when an infected person coughs or sneezes. Symptoms: a cough lasting weeks, weight loss, night sweats, tiredness. It is treated by a **long course of several antibiotics** under a health worker's supervision. The **BCG vaccine** protects young children. Poor ventilation and overcrowding help it spread.

blocks.caption: Three bacterial diseases.
blocks.alt: Three boxes: cholera and typhoid caused by bacteria in dirty water and food, and tuberculosis caused by a bacterium spread by droplets in the air.

blocks.title: Prevention of water-borne disease
blocks.md: Drink **treated or boiled** water; build **latrines** away from wells; wash hands with soap after the toilet and before eating; cover food and keep flies away; wash fruit and vegetables; vaccines exist for cholera and typhoid in some situations. Good sanitation is the most effective protection.

blocks.title: Defence and vaccination
blocks.md:
The body's barriers: **skin**, **mucus and cilia**, **stomach acid**, and **tears**. Inside, **phagocytes** engulf microbes and **lymphocytes** make **antibodies**. A **vaccine** contains dead, weakened or part of a pathogen; the body makes antibodies and **memory cells** without getting ill. If the real pathogen arrives, the **second response is faster and stronger**.

**Antibiotics** kill bacteria, not viruses; misuse leads to resistance.

blocks.caption: Antibody level after first and second exposure (illustrative).
blocks.alt: A graph: the blue curve of the first infection rises slowly to a low peak; the red curve of a second exposure rises faster to a much higher peak.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Antibiotics do not work on viruses (colds, flu, HIV, measles).
- Vaccination does not cure an existing illness; it prepares the body beforehand.
- Boiling is for killing pathogens in water; filtering alone may not remove them.

blocks.title: Rainy-season outbreak
blocks.statement: After floods in a town, many people have watery diarrhoea. Name a likely disease, how it spread and what to give.
steps: Cholera is likely; sewage mixed with drinking water.
Give oral rehydration solution and take the patient to a health centre; stress clean water and handwashing.
blocks.answer: Cholera from contaminated water; oral rehydration and medical care

blocks.title: Reading the antibody graph
blocks.statement: Using the graph above: what is the peak antibody level for the first infection and the second exposure, and how many times higher is the second peak?
steps: First peak is 25 units; second peak is 90 units.
